prompt: Siobhán, the lifecycle marketing manager, thinks affiliate signups activate like everyone else and then fail to upgrade, and asks before Thursday's lifecycle email review where each channel loses the users who signed up in September 2025. Take every user whose signup_ts is from 1 September 2025 00:00 up to but not including 1 October 2025 00:00, UTC. A signup's channel is the channel of the last session of the same visitor_id that started at or before signup_ts: a session with a utm_campaign takes the channel_name of the campaign with that utm_campaign, and a session without one is organic when utm_medium is 'organic', referral when utm_medium is 'referral', and direct otherwise, as when utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign are all missing. When two such sessions start at the same moment, the one with the higher session_id counts as the last. A signup with no such session belongs to a channel named unattributed. A signup is activated when its first_campaign_sent event came no later than 7 days, that is 7 times 24 hours, after signup_ts. A signup is paid when it is activated and the user has a subscription whose start_date is on or before the 30th day after the UTC date of signup_ts; a subscription without that activation does not count. Check each signup's activation within 7 days, and its subscription, with EXISTS or with a join to one row per user from activation_events and subscriptions, so the query stays fast. Return one row for each channel that has at least one of these signups, with seven columns in this order: channel; signups; activated; paid; activation_rate_pct, 100 times activated divided by signups; paid_rate_pct, 100 times paid divided by activated, missing when activated is 0; and overall_rate_pct, 100 times paid divided by signups. Round the three rates to 1 decimal. Sort by overall_rate_pct from high to low, then by channel from A to Z.
hints: Next, take the September 2025 signups and find when each one's last session at or before signing up started, so each signup gets exactly one channel.
Give each signup a 1 or 0 for each step with a check for a matching row, make the paid check require the activated one, and guard the division by the activated count against 0.
why_this_works: Each signup gets one channel from its last session before signing up, and a step counts only for users who passed the step before it.
